# FM cockpit state-dot, pulse and health primitives (reduced-motion honored)

## Context

T1.4 design-system leaf of Epic neomjs/neo-agent-institution#10 (map v1.1) — the smallest visual primitives every fleet surface composes: the agent state dot (with the live-pulse animation), the family rail, and the health-summary swatches. Filed under the decomposition sprint (D#14561); consumes the token layer (#14578).

## The Problem

The SSOT artifact defines these as raw CSS (`.dot` + `@keyframes pulse` gated behind `prefers-reduced-motion`, `.agent::before` family rail, `.sw` swatches). Without a component-level primitive, every view leaf re-implements them — the exact per-view accretion the epic exists to kill — and the anti-lock-in render rules (ADR 0032 §2.3) would be re-derived per consumer instead of enforced once.

## The Architectural Reality

- Neo functional/component primitives under the target namespace (#14577 gate decides placement); these are leaf components/mixins consuming neomjs/neo#14578 tokens only — zero hand-rolled colors.
- ADR 0032 bindings enforced HERE once: the family rail binds an **episode attribute** (data-driven, never a per-agent constant — a family switch re-renders the rail, same resident); state encodes SESSION state (working/idle/wedged/limited/benched — never identity).
- `prefers-reduced-motion` gating is carried from the artifact (pulse is decoration, not information — the dot's color carries the signal).

## The Fix

One PR, the per-view triplet: (1) the primitives (StateDot w/ optional pulse, FamilyRail binding, HealthSwatch) as reusable components/mixins; (2) unit specs (state→token mapping, episode-attribute binding, reduced-motion config path); (3) a minimal NL-verifiable render surface (the primitives mounted in the dev-server, inspectable via Neural Link).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] StateDot renders all five states from neomjs/neo#14578 tokens; pulse only when live AND motion allowed (`prefers-reduced-motion` honored via the artifact's gating).
- [ ] FamilyRail binds a data field (episode attribute), not a constant; changing the bound value re-renders in place (ADR 0032 §2.3.3 fixture).
- [ ] HealthSwatch set renders the five categories; zero hand-rolled color values anywhere (tokens only — lint-greppable).
- [ ] Unit specs cover the three primitives' config→render mapping (custom playwright config, never default `npx playwright test`).
- [ ] NL-verifiable render surface exists (wire-binding slice of the triplet).

## Out of Scope

- The AgentCard composition (T2.7 consumes these) · the health summary BAR layout (T2.8) · token values (#14578).

* fix(agentos): familyToken guards the closed set against prototype-shaped keys (#14635)

@neo-fable's #14722 pre-review reproduced it: familyToken used FAMILY_TOKEN[k]
|| fallback, so a prototype-shaped key (toString / constructor / __proto__)
returned the inherited Object.prototype member (truthy) instead of the neutral
fallback. Delegated to the existing isKnownFamily() hasOwn check so the closed
set stays closed. Regression assertions added (familyToken + isKnownFamily on
toString/constructor/__proto__). 4/4 green.

Systemic: the same MAP[k] || pattern is in kindToken/kindLabel (#14701),
stateLabel (#14726), and stateToken (StateDot, merged) — hardening those in
their PRs + a StateDot follow-up."

* feat(agentos): fleet cockpit HealthSwatch primitive — legend + count-bar unit (#14637)

The last split from the #14593 triplet per review, built to its full ACs

- state → --fm-state-* dot + label via the MERGED StateDot's shared stateToken

* fix(agentos): harden state closed sets against prototype-shaped keys (#14637)

stateToken (shared from StateDot) and stateLabel (HealthSwatch) used `MAP[k] || fallback`, which returns an inherited Object.prototype member for a prototype-shaped key — so state 'toString' / 'constructor' / '__proto__' leaked a function/object into the --fm-dot binding and the swatch label instead of degrading to the neutral off token / literal text.

Both resolvers now use an `Object.hasOwn` closed-set check (the same guard FamilyRail carries). Regression coverage added at the resolver level in both specs, plus a HealthSwatch render case proving both axes (dot token via stateToken, label via stateLabel) are closed-set-safe."
